steps: Unpack + free the barrier screen
Remove the certified barrier screen from the shipping pallet; it must be installed before the stove is operated. Lift off the top plate and release the two glass frame latches to open the firebox.

1. The barrier is secured to the shipping pallet. Remove the two screws and use pliers to break off the perforated shipping straps from both screen frame attachment brackets.
  2. Lift the top plate straight off the stove body.
  3. Open the firebox: pull each glass frame latch handle forward to clear the latch from the notch in the frame.
  4. Read the installation requirements before starting.

Hardware bag

Fuel Conversion Kit - LP156005
Decorative pipe mounting brackets (4)129469
Rock wool, .006 kg224136

Do not operate the stove if any part has been under water. It must not be connected to a chimney or flue serving any other appliance.
Convert to propane (LP only)
Shipped for natural gas. For propane, convert with kit #156005 before the stove is installed: burner and pilot orifices, regulator tower, labels. Authorized service technician only.

Tools: 1/2" open ended wrench or deep-well socket, Torx T20 or slotted screwdriver, 4 mm allen wrench.

  1. Turn off the gas supply. Remove the top plate; release the two glass frame latches and lift the glass panel up and out.
  2. Remove the embers and log set (fragile), then lift out the burner skirt.
  3. Remove the air shutter wingnut from its stud under the stove. Pull the air shutter forward and lift the burner plate and shutter out as a unit (no screws hold the burner).
  4. Change the burner orifice in its brass elbow housing (1/2" wrench or deep-well socket).
  5. Refit the air shutter pushed all the way back; reattach the wingnut and gasket loosely. Refit the burner plate engaged with the shutter and the two front support brackets, pushed toward the rear.
  6. Pull the pilot head straight up; unscrew the pilot orifice with the 4 mm hex key and fit the new one tight and flush with the base to prevent bypass leaks. Push the pilot head back on.
  7. With a Torx T-20, remove the three regulator screws and the tower, gasket, white plastic disk and spring. Fit the new regulator with its gasket positioned; tighten securely.
  8. Labels: A on the back of the stove, B on the rating plate, the small label on the valve.
  9. Reassemble, apply gas and leak-test with soapy water or an electronic gas detector, never an open flame. Check pressures with a manometer.
  10. Set the air shutter: start with the stem at the half-way position in the slot; back restricts air, forward opens it.
Location, hearth + clearances
Out of traffic, away from furniture and drapes, with service access. Not directly on carpet, vinyl, linoleum or Pergo®; hold the listed clearances and alcove limits.

Consider heat distribution, vent termination, gas supply line routing, and traffic areas, furniture and draperies. Provide adequate access around the stove for servicing and operation.

  • Floor protection, clearances and alcove limits: see the spec cards (pp. 6–7). Mantel and trim clearances are a diagram (Fig. 4, p. 7).
  • Combustible means anything that can burn, including materials behind non-combustibles. "Fire resistant" materials and fire-rated sheet rock are considered combustible.

Mobile home (p. 23)

  • Secure the stove to the floor with Jøtul Floor Bracket Kit #750304.
  • Provide an electrical ground between the stove and the mobile home chassis.
  • Install per Title 24 CFR, Part 3280 in the U.S.; in Canada, CSA Z240.4. Check local restrictions.
Vent system
4" Type B or listed flex gas liner, vertical termination only: 7 – 35 ft, max 4 ft total horizontal run, max three 90° or four 45° elbows. Never shared with another appliance.

• Through combustible walls and ceilings: Type B with listed clearances and the approved 4" Simpson Dura-Vent wall thimble (the manual prints its number two ways: see the Venting spec card). Firestop at every floor.
  • Roof: flashing, storm collar, thimble and Type B cap; termination height per the Gas Vent Rule (Fig. 5).
  • Above 2000': minimum vertical rise 12' from the draft hood.

Decorative pipe (optional, p. 17)

None is supplied; the four locator brackets in the hardware bag center it over the draft hood. Remove the four 1/4" hex head screws holding the 4" flue collar to the draft hood (leave the collar on), align the "L" brackets with the holes and refit the screws. With 6" decorative pipe over the venting, a listed flexible gas liner must connect directly to the draft hood. Never use single wall stove pipe as the vent.
Gas supply connection
3/8" npt at the left side of the front-mounted valve, with a 1/2" diameter supply or sized to hold pressure at any input. Shut-off valve (gas cock) and union in the same room.

• Supply line 3/8" npt with a 1/2" diameter supply, or the size that gives sufficient gas pressure to the valve regardless of the input setting.
  • Gas shut-off valve (gas cock) and union in the supply line, in the same room as the stove. Massachusetts: T-handle gas cock (248CMR), and the stove must be installed by a licensed master or journeyman plumber or gas-fitter (p. 2).
  • Flexible gas appliance connectors are acceptable in many U.S. areas; Canadian methods vary with local code.
  • Seal all joints; on propane, use propane-resistant compounds. Comply with local code, or ANSI Z223.1/NFPA 54 or CAN-B149.
  • The suggested tools list an external regulator for propane only, and a sediment trap if required by code (p. 2).
Note: p. 13 says to install the optional blower before connecting the gas line, to ensure adequate clearance between the two; p. 20 says to connect the gas supply line before installing the blower, with a 90° elbow off the control valve for clearance.
Leak test + gas pressures
Leak-test every joint with soapy water, never a flame. Manometer on test point E (inlet) and A (manifold) with the valve control knob on HIGH.

Leak test

  1. Mix a 50-50 solution of water and dish soap.
  2. Light the stove (lighting instructions on the inside back cover or the rating plate).
  3. Brush or spray all joints and connections.
  4. Bubbles or a gas odor: turn the gas control knob to OFF immediately, tighten or reconnect the joint, and retest.

Pressure test

Gauge connections are on the front of the valve under the On/Off/Pilot knob: E inlet (supply), A manifold. Always test with the valve control knob set on HIGH.

Inlet NG / LP5.0 – 7.0 / 12.0 – 14.9 in. WC
Manifold NG / LP1.2 – 3.8 / 2.9 – 11.0 in. WC
Supply piping tests above 1/2 psig (3.5 kPa): disconnect the appliance and its main gas valve. At 1/2 psig or less: isolate it by closing its manual shut-off valve.
Log set + embers
Install the five-piece log set before operating the burner, wearing gloves. Spread ember stones loosely; keep the pilot opening clear and embers 1/4" from the burner skirt edges.

The logs and a bag of ember stones are packed inside the firebox. Wear gloves: the ceramic fibers irritate skin. Placement is shown in Figs. 20–24:

  1. Right log: the holes in its underside go onto the peg in the burner skirt.
  2. Rear log: the holes go onto the two pegs in the burner skirt.
  3. Left log, then left middle log, then top log.
  • Spread embers evenly over the burner plate and around the logs. Do not obstruct the pilot assembly opening or pile embers against the burner skirt edges (keep 1/4" clearance).
  • Not all the embers are needed; too many can promote sooting on the logs.

Optional Antique Brick Panel Kit #155375: install it before the log set (procedure p. 22).

The manual prints the brick kit number as 155370 on p. 15; p. 22 and the accessories list on p. 25 give #155375.
Thermostat or remote (optional)
750 millivolt DC two-wire thermostat only: minimum 16 gauge wire, maximum 25 feet, to the two left terminals above the ignitor button. Rocker switch to T-STAT; the pilot powers it.

• Thermostat in the same room as the stove, typically 5 feet off the floor, away from drafts.
  • Minimum 16 gauge wire, maximum 25 feet.
  • Connect the two leads to the two left terminals on the terminal block directly above the ignitor button. Don't overtighten; no other wires need disconnecting. At the thermostat, use the two screws on the base plate.
  • The On/Off/T-Stat switch on the back of the stove goes to T-STAT, and the pilot must be running: it is the thermostat's power source.
  • Remote receiver: wire it to the terminal block the same way; follow the remote's own instructions.
Critical: the red thermopile wire must be connected to the valve TH/TP terminal to power the thermostat. Label all wires before disconnecting them when servicing the controls.

Accessories: wall thermostat 750003, remote control 750002 (p. 25).
System check + air shutter
Purge the gas line, verify the pilot flame, run HI/LOW and look for soot. If the flame is weak or sooty, a qualified gas technician adjusts the air shutter.

1. Purge: the first lighting takes a few moments to clear air from the gas line.
  2. Pilot (view port at the rear of the right log): steady, not lifting or floating; blue around the pilot hood with traces of yellow toward the outer edges; engulfs the top 3/8" of the thermopile and the top 1/8" of the thermocouple; projects 1" out of the pilot hood at all three ports.
  3. Burner: HI/LOW knob in the center of the valve face; up to 50% adjustment between LOW and HIGH.
  4. No smoke or soot. Check log placement first; if it persists, adjust the air shutter. The more offsets in the vent system, the greater the need for adjustment.

Air shutter (p. 16)

  1. Under the right side of the stove, loosen the wingnut closest to you. Slide the stud forward to open, back for less air, in small increments.
  2. Tighten the wingnut at the desired setting.
  3. Burn 30 minutes on HIGH, watching the flame; if weak, slow or sooty, repeat.

Too large an opening: a blue, transparent "anemic" flame. Too small: very long yellow flames and soot. Fig. 29 shows the flame on high after approximately 15 to 20 minutes.

light.title: Lighting the pilot
light.html:
This stove has a standing pilot that you light by hand. Once lit, the pilot keeps burning, and the ON/OFF switch runs the main burner. The same steps are on the stove's rating plate.

  1. Read the safety information first, including what to do if you smell gas.
  2. Get to the lower controls.
  3. Turn the stove's ON/OFF switch to OFF, or set the thermostat to its lowest setting if you use one.
  4. Check that the shut-off valve on the gas supply line is open.
  5. Push the gas control knob in slightly and turn it clockwise to OFF. Don't force it.
  6. Wait five minutes to clear out any gas. If you then smell gas, stop and follow the gas-smell steps.
  7. Push the knob in slightly and turn it counterclockwise to PILOT.
  8. Push the knob all the way in and hold it. Right away, press the red spark button repeatedly until the pilot lights. Keep holding the knob for about one minute, then let go. It should spring back, and the pilot should stay lit. If it goes out, repeat steps 5 to 8.
  9. Turn the knob counterclockwise to ON.
  10. Turn the ON/OFF switch to ON, or set the thermostat to the temperature you want.
Stop and call your service technician or gas supplier if the knob doesn't spring back when you let go, or if the pilot won't stay lit after several tries (turn the knob to OFF first). Turn the knob by hand only, never with tools.

burner.title: Turning the burner on and off
burner.html:
Once the pilot is lit, the main burner is controlled by the rocker switch at the left corner of the rear shroud, at the back of the stove.

ON / OFFyou turn the burner on and off by hand
T-STATan optional wall thermostat or remote control runs the burner

Flame height

Turn the HI/LOW knob in the center of the gas valve face. You can adjust the fire up to 50% between LOW and HIGH. Don't try to change the flame by setting the gas control knob anywhere other than full ON.

Turning it off

  • Day to day: turn the ON/OFF switch to OFF. The burner goes out and the pilot stays lit.
  • Complete shutdown: turn the switch to OFF, get to the lower controls, then push the gas control knob in slightly and turn it clockwise to OFF. Don't force it.
Using a thermostat or remote? The pilot has to be burning, because it powers the thermostat. For the remote, follow the instructions that come with it.

firstfire.title: That smell, fog or sound is probably normal
firstfire.html:
An odor or a little smoke

During the first few fires you may notice an odor or some smoke. That's normal: manufacturing residue is burning off and the materials are curing. Extra ventilation and fresh air near the stove help it pass.

Foggy glass

Condensation may form on the glass each time you light the stove. The fog disappears as the stove heats up.

Creaking and pinging

Cast iron and steel expand and contract as the temperature changes. The creaks and pings you hear are that natural movement.

A low hum

If you have the optional blower, it hums slightly on its low setting, and the sound grows as the fan speeds up.

The very first lighting takes a few moments while air clears out of the gas line. Later starts don't need this unless the gas supply line has been shut off.
A gas smell is different. Don't light anything, don't touch electrical switches, and don't use any phone in your building. Call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the glass only when it needs it, and only when the stove is cool.

  1. Wipe the glass with a clean, damp, soft cloth.
  2. Follow with a dry, soft towel.
  3. Take care not to scratch the surface.
Never use abrasive cleaners on the glass, and never clean it while it's hot.

Handle it with care

  • The glass panel can shatter unexpectedly if something strikes it. Don't slam or strike it.
  • Never run the stove with the glass removed, cracked or broken.
  • Replacement glass should be fitted by a licensed or qualified service person, using only Jøtul ceramic glass replacement kit 155599.

The glass gasket should be inspected at least once a year to make sure it still seals well.

flame.title: What a good flame looks like
flame.html:
The pilot

You can see the pilot through the view port at the rear of the right log. It should be steady, not lifting or floating. It should be blue around the pilot hood, with traces of yellow toward the outer edges.

The main flames

There should be no smoke or soot. The air shutter sets how much air mixes with the gas, and two signs tell you it's off:

  • Blue and see-through, an "anemic" flame: the air opening is too large.
  • Very long and yellow, with soot: the air setting is too small. Soot shows up as black deposits on the logs, on the inside walls of the stove, and possibly on the vent cap outside.

If you see soot or smoke, the log placement should be checked first. If it continues, the air shutter may need adjusting. Too many ember stones can also cause soot on the logs.

Leave the air shutter to a pro. Only a qualified gas technician should adjust it.

spill.title: When the burner shuts itself off
spill.html:
Your stove has a spill switch, also called a blocked flue switch. If the vent system becomes blocked, it shuts off the burner.

  • It's on the side of the draft hood, at the back of the stove.
  • Press its reset button to let the burner work again.
If it keeps shutting the burner off, turn off the gas supply and call your dealer or service technician. The switch will keep shutting off the burner until the vent problem is fixed.

Not every vent problem can be fixed. Stoves vented this way (B-vent) are affected by outdoor air conditions and by air pressure inside the house. Steep roofs, nearby trees and windy sites can cause poor draft or downdrafts; a taller vent or a high-wind cap may help. Ask your dealer or installer.

blower.title: The optional blower
blower.html:
The optional variable-speed blower (#156000) moves more heat from around the firebox out into the room.

AUTOa heat-sensing switch (snapstat) starts the blower once the fire has been burning for a while
MANUALuse it if you don't want the blower to run automatically
Speed knobturn it to set the fan speed

In AUTO, if the burner turns off, the blower shuts off by itself once the stove cools down. The snapstat only works with the control switch in AUTO.

The blower has a three-prong grounding plug. Plug it directly into a properly grounded three-prong outlet, and never cut or remove the grounding prong. Unplug it before any service work on the stove.

safety.title: Safety around the stove
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Put out any open flame and open windows.
  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Call your gas supplier right away from a neighbor's phone and follow their instructions.
  • If you can't reach your gas supplier, call the fire department.

Around the stove

  • The stove gets very hot. Everyone should stay away from hot surfaces to avoid burns or clothing catching fire. Supervise young children in the room.
  • Keep the barrier screen that came with the stove in place: it reduces the risk of burns from the hot glass. Put it back after any service, and if it's damaged, replace it with the manufacturer's barrier for this stove, part 157715.
  • Keep clothing and anything flammable away. Never store or use gasoline or other flammable liquids nearby.
  • Burn natural gas or propane only, never wood, paper, cardboard or coal.
  • Don't use the stove if any part has been under water. Call a qualified service technician.
The manual's safety page prints the replacement barrier as PN 157699 (p. 6); its parts list gives 157715 for the Safety Screen Barrier (p. 25).
Massachusetts: a carbon monoxide detector must be installed in the same room as the stove.

service.title: Annual service
service.html:
Have a qualified service technician inspect the stove and its vent system before use and at least once a year.

The yearly checklist in the manual

  • The whole vent system, chimney included, inspected and cleaned.
  • Firebox, valve compartment, air passages and optional blower checked so air flows freely.
  • Firebox vacuumed with a soft brush attachment; the logs are fragile.
  • Pilot head, thermopile and thermocouple (the parts the pilot flame touches) checked for rust or wear.
  • Burner ports checked for blockages, especially around the pilot.
  • Glass gasket checked for wear and a good seal.

Between visits

Keep the controls and the area under the stove free of debris, and vacuum there often, but only when the stove is cold. Lint from carpets or bedding can mean the stove needs cleaning more often.

Before any service work, turn off the gas supply and unplug the blower.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Jøtul's limited warranty covers the original retail purchaser, from the date of purchase:

Cast iron, steel doors, surround parts, firebox5 years
Burner, burner treatments, firebox panels2 years
Enamel finish (peeling or fading)2 years
Gas and electrical parts (controls, plumbing, valve, blower)1 year

What voids or limits it

  • Installation or service by anyone other than an authorized installer, service agency or gas supplier, or not following the manual and local codes.
  • Damage from unauthorized changes, use or repair, or damage in transit.
  • Normal wear parts such as gaskets and glass, unless thermal stress damaged them.
  • Enamel damage from improper use, such as bubbling, cracking or discoloring.
To make a claim, contact your nearest authorized Jøtul dealer. Jøtul must get notice of a possible defect within 60 days of when it was first found. Keep your dated sales receipt. The warranty can't be transferred.
Note: the manual describes where the rating plate (it carries your serial number) is in three ways: it hangs on the back (p. 3), is attached to the bottom of the stove (p. 17), and is attached to the burner assembly (p. 18).

specVent.title: Venting
specVent.html:
Atmospherically vented, vertical termination only, directly to the outside. 4" Type B vent pipe or a listed flexible gas liner, not less than or greater than 4" in diameter.

Vertical height7 ft min · 35 ft max
Above 2000' altitudemin. vertical rise 12' from the draft hood
Total horizontal run4 ft max (distance between 45° elbows counts)
Horizontal slope1/4" per foot up toward the cap
Elbowsmax three 90° or four 45°; 45° preferred
Offsetssupport the pipe every three feet
  • No horizontal termination, nothing below the roof eaves. Roof: flashing, storm collar, thimble and Type B cap.
  • Through combustible walls and ceilings: Type B with listed clearances and the 4" Dura-Vent wall thimble only. Firestop at every floor; venting exposed above the first floor must be enclosed.
  • Unused masonry flue: reline with 4" Type B or a listed flexible gas liner; the space around the liner can't vent another appliance. Venting through a thimble into a masonry flue: any venting exposed in the room must be Type B, or a flexible liner sleeved in 24 ga. 6" stove pipe. Flexible liners may not be exposed in any living space.
  • No single wall connector pipe. Never attach to a chimney serving a solid fuel or gas appliance.
  • Steep roofs, nearby trees, wind: poor draft or downdraft; a taller vent or high-wind cap may help. A chimney outside the building envelope may downdraft or reverse flow; a basement B-vent to one is not recommended.

specHearth.title: Floor protection
specHearth.html:
The GF 400 BV cannot be installed directly on carpeting, vinyl, linoleum or Pergo®.

  • On any combustible material other than wood, install a floor pad that is metal or wood, or a listed hearth pad.
  • The floor protection must extend the full width and depth of the stove.
  • Carpeting, vinyl or linoleum need not be removed from under the floor protection.

Minimum hearth protection is shown as a diagram (Fig. 1).

specConv.title: Fuel conversion and high altitude
specConv.html:
Shipped forNatural gas only
Natural gas to propaneKit 156005 (supplied)
Propane back to natural gasKit 156006 (order)
Burner orifice3.20 mm NG · #49 LP
Pilot orifice#51 NG · #30 LP

Convert before the stove is installed, by an authorized service technician. The kit holds a regulator tower labeled for propane with 3 screws, the orifices, Label A (back of stove), Label B (rating plate) and a small valve label. After conversion the air shutter may need adjustment.

High altitude (p. 23)

Natural gas at 2000 - 4500 ft. (610 M - 1370 M) requires compensation; consult the local gas distributor or authority having jurisdiction for rating methods. Kits: #155895 NG, #155885-LP. Follow steps 1-10 of the conversion procedure, fit the kit orifice (3.10 mm NG or #51 LP), fill out the high altitude label and attach it to the rating plate or gas valve, reassemble, and adjust the air shutter if needed.

Note: on propane at high altitude, p. 23 says "Do not derate the burner for propane", yet p. 23 also lists High Altitude Kit #155885-LP and a #51 LP orifice, and p. 25 lists the LP kit 155885 in the accessories.

review.notes: No troubleshooting chart or code table in the manual: fault panels are built from the fault descriptions on pp. 8-9, 15-18 and 27; codes left empty. Figure-only content not transcribed: the dimension drawing (p. 4), minimum hearth protection (Fig. 1, p. 6), corner placement (Fig. 3, p. 7) and mantel/trim clearances (Fig. 4, p. 7). Because the p. 4 drawing labels can't be read from the text, the catalog height, width and depth couldn't be checked; catalog heating area and weight aren't in the manual. BTU, efficiency (63.51%, CSA P.4.1-15), vent size, blower, mobile home approval and standing pilot all match. Short scrambled figure labels on pp. 7, 8 and 14 don't decode with the 29-code-point rule (either direction) and were not used. French text on pp. 11, 21 and 23 repeats the English warnings; nothing is French-only, and the gas-smell block is in English. Manual copy errors (not used in the guide): p. 13 points to Gas Pressure on page 15 (it's p. 14); p. 22 points to the log set on page 21 (it's p. 15); p. 19 refers to a maintenance form on page 26 (p. 26 is the warranty); p. 23 says the conversion kit comes with the 'GF 300 DV'; pp. 2 and 20 call the stove a fireplace insert; blower step 4 (p. 20) says #7 x 1/2" screws but the kit list says #8 x 1/2"; the Gas Vent Rule table (p. 8) skips 'over 13/12 to 14/12'; Fig. 3 labels 9 1/2" as 251 mm. Glass replacement kit 155599 (p. 19) vs ceramic glass part 220567 (p. 25) read as kit vs part, not flagged. The manual doesn't describe operation during a power outage, so there's no outage tile. Catalog features the manual doesn't support: a 'Linen' finish (the parts list shows Matte Black, Blue Black, Ivory, Jøtul Iron and Majolica finishes) and 'open-door fire viewing' (the manual says never operate with the glass removed). Website check (Oct 12): every website figure the guide shows matches the manual (NG/LP input rates), so no website notes were added. The website's 'Approved for open/closed door fire viewing with Safety Screen Barrier' isn't covered by the manual: the parts list shows cast-iron Left and Right Doors separate from the Glass Frame, and the manual only says not to operate with the glass removed, cracked or broken.
